search_log: Searched "Alexandra Ripley Scarlett 1991 excerpt first chapter", Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive variants; found the licensed LitRes Chapter 1 translation, while Google Books and Open Library offered metadata or restricted previews rather than usable sustained English prose.
Searched "Scarlett Alexandra Ripley point of view", "third person", "narrator", and "narrative perspective"; BookRags explicitly identified third-person omniscient-limited narration.
Searched for epistolary, frame, multiple-narrator, alternating-person, and first-person descriptions; found no structural source establishing sustained narration in another person.

Followed up on a StoryGraph reader's vague claim of third/first switching; the available passages show first-person direct thoughts locally embedded within third-person narration, not autonomous first-person sections.
Searched exact text from q03207-q03209; all three matched Cathy Cassidy's separate 2006 novel Scarlett, explaining the anomalous first-person present-tense material.
person_note: Ripley's base narration is third person, closely focalized mainly through Scarlett. Multiple interior quotes provide sustained third-person scene and consciousness narration, and the licensed Chapter 1 translation independently shows the same structure. First-person wording in q03202 is explicitly Scarlett's local direct thought and does not create an alternating strand. q03207-q03209 are title-collision contamination from Cathy Cassidy's different novel and were excluded from the book-level decision. The main limitation is that the authorized web prose is a translation of one named chapter rather than whole-book English text, but the distributed Ripley quotes and explicit whole-book POV description agree without credible structural contradiction.
